circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One facility, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding later installations in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a Melbourne street circuit that winds around Albert Park Lake, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various support racing categories. The track maintains the highest FIA safety classification for circuit facilities.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Styria, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has undergone significant transformations since its inception as the Österreichring in 1970, when it began hosting the Austrian Grand Prix for nearly two decades. Following a reconstruction and shortening, the venue was renamed and returned to the F1 calendar from 1997 to 2003 as a host of the same Grand Prix event.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street-based racing venue in Azerbaijan measuring 6. 003 km per lap, making it the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The circuit first hosted a Formula One race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before transitioning to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and held the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that same year. The FIA Grade 1-licensed venue accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 Series, endurance racing, and drag racing, while featuring multiple track configurations for different events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km motorsport venue located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, featuring a balanced layout with extended straights and diverse corner configurations. Holding FIA Grade 1 status and equipped with seating for approximately 140,700 spectators, it serves as a comprehensive test of driver skill across multiple racing disciplines.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit, stretching over 7 km through the Ardennes region, has been hosting Formula One's Belgian Grand Prix since 1950 and remains one of the championship's longest-standing venues. The track has maintained continuous Grand Prix status from 1985 onward, with only two cancellations breaking this streak during the 2000s.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometer temporary street circuit that annually hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships and North American open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, with the race returning from 2024 onward. The track also began hosting electric racing events from 2024, expanding its calendar beyond traditional formula motorsport.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Northamptonshire in England, Silverstone Circuit has hosted the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably staged the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After decades of rotating with other venues, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit located near Budapest, Hungary, that hosts the annual Hungarian Grand Prix. Built in just eight months starting in late 1985, it became the venue for Formula One's first race behind the Iron Curtain when it opened on 24 March 1986, constructed as a permanent facility near a major highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were abandoned.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 and ranks among Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venues. The track hosts the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, making it one of the few circuits to appear continuously on the Formula One calendar, and earned its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its characteristic long straights and swift corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda's subsidiary, located in Mie Prefecture with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is primarily recognized as a premier Formula One racing destination and hosts the Japanese Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving around the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its adjoining thoroughfares. The track passes several iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues, including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of the most visually distinctive racing venues in the world.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Mexico City's Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named after brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both accomplished drivers who tragically perished in racing accidents in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix twice before on an earlier configuration, most recently in 1992, before resuming as a regular calendar fixture from 2015 onwards under its current "Mexico City Grand Prix" designation.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: This temporary circuit in Miami Gardens winds around Hard Rock Stadium and spans 3. 363 miles with 19 turns, generating qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 and has since hosted the Miami Grand Prix as its primary event, with Formula E adopting a modified version from the 2025–26 season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the harbor perimeter of the Principality of Monaco. The venue is widely known as Monte Carlo due to the circuit's prominent location within that neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix following its return to Formula One in 2021. The venue's partnership with the sport concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motor racing facility situated north of Doha, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian motorsport venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track features additional facilities including a karting circuit dedicated to fellow racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, positioned along the Red Sea waterfront. Since 2021, it has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and it recently began accommodating a Formula E event starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront area, utilizing the streets surrounding Marina Bay and spanning into the Kallang district.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya near Barcelona spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test of driver and car performance. The Spanish venue holds an FIA Grade 1 classification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix, alongside hosting major events in MotoGP and endurance racing. Beyond its F1 duties, the track has accommodated various international motorsport categories including NASCAR and the Lone Star Le Mans, while previously staging IndyCar and other series competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai-British driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships during his 23-season career with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship and multiple prestigious 24-hour races, making him the sole driver to have secured both Formula One and sportscar world titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined the Mercedes Formula One team in 2025 and has secured eight race victories since entering the championship.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British racing driver currently competing in Formula One for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian racing driver, currently races in Formula One as part of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while competing for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan holds a reserve role at Haas while competing in endurance racing with Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category. He has made seven Formula One race appearances between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Alpine. He previously achieved victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian racing driver currently competing in Formula One as a member of the Red Bull Racing team, representing France in the championship.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, equalling Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple all-time records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi, bringing considerable experience from his motorsport career. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved victory in the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans endurance race in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver represents Ferrari on the Formula One grid and has secured nine race victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver who returned to Formula One for the 2022 season after a two-year absence, competing until 2024. Currently, he focuses on endurance racing as a BMW factory driver with WRT in the World Endurance Championship, while also competing part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship. Over his eight-season career in the sport, he has achieved 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The talented competitor achieved a career milestone by securing victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix during his time with Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Checo Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while competing for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having claimed nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo, known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, bringing with him four Grand Prix victories accumulated throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in the IMSA SportsCar Championship.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing under his commonly used name in the sport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, has held various roles within the Red Bull Racing family since joining Formula One in 2021, including full-time competition and reserve duties. As of 2026, he continues his association with the team in a support capacity.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen is a Dutch and Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, where he has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Over 12 seasons, the Dutch-flagged competitor has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the championship between 2022 and 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position at Cadillac in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed under the Alpine banner since 2021, serving as Renault's factory operation after rebranding from the Renault F1 Team to highlight the Alpine sports car marque. Renault maintained its works team status through the 2025 season before withdrawing from Formula One competition.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has maintained a presence in Formula One through different configurations over time, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding in the championship.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the Italian luxury automaker's racing operations and remains Formula One's most storied competitor, having participated continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The team's iconic emblem has earned it the affectionate moniker "the Prancing Horse," and it holds the distinction of being both the longest-tenured and most accomplished outfit in the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR entrepreneur Gene Haas debuted on the grid in 2016, establishing itself as a competitive midfield presence over subsequent seasons. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal position, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had overseen operations since the team's creation in 2014.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm competed in Formula One from 1993 until 2025, becoming the sport's fourth-longest-running independent constructor by race count. The team achieved significant success in endurance racing, including overall victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours, before establishing itself as a regular grid presence through multiple iterations and ownership changes. Audi acquired the organization in 2024 to serve as the foundation for its upcoming factory team entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a division of the McLaren Group, with full ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a team owner and engine supplier, with its current incarnation based in Brackley and operating under a German racing licence. The team, now known as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, saw its ownership structure evolve in January 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside the Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff. Mercedes-branded entries have traditionally carried the "Silver Arrows" nickname throughout their racing history.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad represents the conglomerate's second constructor entry in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as Red Bull GmbH's second team entry alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a Milton Keynes facility, the outfit operates as a sister team within the Austrian conglomerate's Formula One portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing operates as an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England, established in 2005 as one of two racing operations within the Red Bull GmbH portfolio. Christian Horner led the organization from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies assuming the team principal role thereafter.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, currently competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier unsuccessful racing venture. Headquartered on a 60-acre site in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has operated as both competitor and chassis manufacturer throughout its Formula One history.
